sentence: This project studies why hematopoietic stem cells lose function after bone marrow transplantation and how they can be kept working.
This project improves an open-source platform that measures human movement using videos from smartphones and builds a video-based balance test.
This project tries to predict which pathways are disrupted in a cancer using only its DNA sequence.
This project studies how Pseudomonas aeruginosa uses mechanical cues to detect surface contact and form biofilms, using microfluidic tools and single cell microscopy.
This project uses machine learning on electronic health record data to find patients who have hypertrophic cardiomyopathy but were never diagnosed.
This project develops point-of-care and home-based diagnostics, covering their development, assessment and manufacturing.
This project builds tools that measure epigenetic and transcriptomic features in single cells.
This project tests whether artificial intelligence can accurately find women at high risk of breast cancer, using mammography screening across the United States.
This project studies how a protein regulates the formation of the palate and how losing it contributes to a cleft palate.
This project tries to find out how an imbalance in the gut microbiome leads to systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction.
This project combines long-read sequencing methods to study protein-coding genes in complex regions of duplication that are difficult to sequence.
This project studies how a histone demethylase drives small cell lung cancer, using cell lines and mouse models.
This project builds a way to measure many more protein markers at once in tissue imaging, using immunostaining and fluorescence imaging.
This project keeps and shares a collection of induced pluripotent stem cell lines for research on Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias.
This project studies how zinc controls processes that sperm go through between mating and fertilization.
This project uses computer modeling to work out high-resolution 3D structures of chromosomes.
This project studies how inherited genetic variants and tumor-specific genetic variants that occur together in tumors affect disease risk and outcome.
This project develops ultrasmall nanoparticles that deliver bioactive peptides into osteocytes to activate signaling pathways for treating osteoporosis.
This project develops reagents that bind a target protein and also cleave it, at lower cost than antibodies.
This project uses single-cell transcriptomics and mutant mouse models to study the mechanisms of neural tube defects.
